Architecture Diagram

The application is a server-rendered ASP.NET MVC photo gallery. It stores image blobs in Azure Blob Storage and has no relational database or separate service tier.

Data Storage & External Services

Images are stored as block blobs in an Azure Blob Storage container named webappstoragedotnet-imagecontainer. The sample configures UseDevelopmentStorage=true, indicating a local storage emulator endpoint for development; no database, cache, message broker, or other external API is evident.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • MVC routes, controller actions, and Razor views are combined in a single web application.
  • The controller directly uses the Azure Blob Storage SDK; a separate service or repository layer is not present.
  • Blob storage is the durable data store, and the application lists, uploads, and deletes blobs through the storage client.

DTOs & Contracts

No dedicated request or response DTO classes, OpenAPI specification, protobuf schema, or GraphQL schema are declared. The gallery action passes a List as its view model; upload uses the MVC request file collection, and delete accepts a form parameter. No immutable DTO contracts are present. The application uses MVC/Razor view rendering rather than a separately documented JSON API.

Communication Patterns

Browser requests and controller responses use synchronous HTTP. The controller makes asynchronous SDK calls for upload and deletion, and synchronously enumerates blobs for gallery listing and bulk deletion. There are no additional application services, API gateway, message broker, service discovery, client-side load balancing, explicit retry policy, circuit breaker, or fallback policy identified. The application configuration does not define API-level authentication, authorization, or TLS; these controls are not established by the inspected project configuration.

Core Business Workflows

The application provides a simple photo gallery for browsing, uploading, and removing images. Gallery items are represented by image blobs, with Azure Blob Storage as the source of truth.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
GalleryWebApp-Storage-DotNet / Photo GalleryA user-facing collection of stored imagesContains image blobs
Image BlobWebApp-Storage-DotNet / Photo GalleryAn image object available for display or removalBelongs to the gallery container

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
WebApp-Storage-DotNetPhoto GalleryGallery interactions and image blob namingAzure Blob Storage

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse the Gallery

  1. A visitor requests the gallery page.
  2. The application initializes the configured blob container if needed and lists its blobs.
  3. The application selects block blobs, converts them to image URIs, and renders the gallery.
  4. If storage access fails, the application displays its error view.

Workflow 2: Upload Images

  1. A visitor selects one or more files and submits the upload form.
  2. The application checks whether the request contains files.
  3. For each file, it creates a unique blob name from the current tick count, a GUID, and the original extension, then uploads it.
  4. The visitor is redirected to the gallery after completion; an exception displays the error view.

Workflow 3: Remove Images

  1. A visitor submits a delete action for one image or all images.
  2. The application derives the blob name from the supplied image URI for a single deletion, or iterates through the container for bulk deletion.
  3. Only block blobs are selected for bulk deletion; individual deletion uses delete-if-present behavior.
  4. The visitor is redirected to the gallery after completion; an exception displays the error view.

Cross-Service Data Flows

There is no service-to-service composition. The web application is the only application service and directly reads and mutates blob data in Azure Blob Storage. No fallback data source or degraded cross-service response is configured.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Visitor as "Gallery Visitor" participant App as "Gallery Application" participant Storage as "Blob Storage" Visitor->>App: Open gallery App->>Storage: Ensure container and list blobs alt Storage responds Storage-->>App: Stored image blobs App-->>Visitor: Render gallery images else Storage operation fails Storage-->>App: Storage error App-->>Visitor: Display error view end Visitor->>App: Submit selected image files alt Files are selected App->>App: Generate unique blob names App->>Storage: Upload each image Storage-->>App: Upload result App-->>Visitor: Redirect to gallery else No files are selected App-->>Visitor: Redirect to gallery end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Only block blobs are included in the gallery and in the bulk-delete operation.
  • Each uploaded object receives a generated name using timestamp ticks and a GUID, while retaining the source file extension.
  • Single-image deletion is conditional on the blob existing; bulk deletion visits blobs in the container.
  • No file-type, content, size, or user-authorization business checks are evident in the inspected workflow. No transaction, audit trail, or multi-service consistency mechanism is configured.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The application targets .NET Framework 4.8 and uses ASP.NET MVC 5.2.3; this is a legacy, Windows/IIS-oriented stack rather than an ASP.NET Core application. Several declared browser and serialization dependencies are old, including jQuery 1.10.2, Newtonsoft.Json 6.0.8, and Microsoft.Net.Compilers 1.0.0. Migration compatibility should be assessed package by package, especially for the legacy OData libraries.

Notable Observations

  • The package manifest declares six browser-facing packages, including older jQuery and Bootstrap releases.
  • Both Newtonsoft.Json and System.Text.Json are declared; the project may carry overlapping serialization capabilities.
  • Microsoft.Data.Edm, Microsoft.Data.OData, Microsoft.Data.Services.Client, and System.Spatial form an older OData-related dependency group.
  • No central package management file, lock file, or test-scoped package dependency is present.
